name: NodeVulnerabilities
description: Known vulnerabilities in the software the cluster runs on: the Kubernetes API server, the kubelet and the container runtime.

controls.name: Kubernetes API server has known vulnerabilities
controls.description: Detects when the Kubernetes API server version has known vulnerabilities at or above the configured minimum severity.
controls.long_description: The Kubernetes API server is part of the cluster itself, so a known vulnerability in it is exposed regardless of how well the workloads are configured. Kubescape reads the Kubernetes API server version from the Kubernetes API and matches it against the same vulnerability database used for image scanning. Kubernetes CVEs are attributed to a component only when the official Kubernetes CVE feed lists it as affected, so a vulnerability in another component, or one limited to another operating system, does not fail this control. Versions that cannot be assessed are reported as coverage gaps rather than as passed.
controls.remediation: Upgrade the control plane to a Kubernetes patch release that fixes the listed vulnerabilities.
controls.test: Checks the vulnerabilities found for the Kubernetes API server version, filtered by the configured minimum severity, fix availability and vendor build settings.

rules.name: component-vulnerabilities-api-server

controlConfigInputs.name: Minimum severity
controlConfigInputs.description: The lowest vulnerability severity that fails the control: Negligible, Low, Medium, High or Critical.

controlConfigInputs.name: Only vulnerabilities with a fix
controlConfigInputs.description: When true, only vulnerabilities with a fixed version available fail the control.

controlConfigInputs.name: Count vendor builds
controlConfigInputs.description: When true, vulnerabilities in vendor builds (for example EKS, GKE or AKS versions) fail the control. Vendors may backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so these findings are not counted by default.

rules.description: Fails when the Kubernetes API server version has known vulnerabilities at or above the configured minimum severity.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the control plane to a Kubernetes patch release that fixes the listed vulnerabilities.
rules.rule:
# regal ignore:directory-package-mismatch
package armo_builtins

import rego.v1

deny contains msga if {
	some res in input
	res.apiVersion == "componentvulns.kubescape.cloud/v1beta0"
	res.kind == "APIServerVulnerabilities"
	counted_assessment(res)

	failing := [i | some i, v in res.data.vulnerabilities; reportable(v)]
	count(failing) > 0
	vuln_paths := [sprintf("data.vulnerabilities[%d]", [i]) | some i in failing]

	msga := {
		"alertMessage": sprintf("kube-apiserver %v has known vulnerabilities: %v", [res.data.version, concat(", ", [res.data.vulnerabilities[i].id | some i in failing])]),
		"packagename": "armo_builtins",
		"alertScore": 8,
		"reviewPaths": vuln_paths,
		"failedPaths": vuln_paths,
		"fixPaths": [],
		"alertObject": {"k8sApiObjects": [res]},
	}
}

counted_assessment(res) if res.data.assessment == "verified"

counted_assessment(res) if {
	res.data.assessment == "vendor-build"
	enabled("componentVulnCountVendorBuilds")
}

reportable(v) if {
	severity_rank(v.severity) >= min_severity_rank(data.postureControlInputs)
	fix_requirement_met(v)
}

fix_requirement_met(_) if not enabled("componentVulnOnlyWithFix")

fix_requirement_met(v) if v.fixState == "fixed"

enabled(name) if lower(data.postureControlInputs[name][_]) == "true"

severity_rank(s) := object.get(
	{"negligible": 1, "low": 2, "medium": 3, "high": 4, "critical": 5},
	lower(s),
	0,
)

min_severity_rank(inputs) := min(ranks) if {
	ranks := [r | some s in inputs.componentVulnMinSeverity; r := severity_rank(s); r > 0]
	count(ranks) > 0
} else := severity_rank("High")

controls.name: Kubelet has known vulnerabilities
controls.description: Detects nodes whose kubelet version has known vulnerabilities at or above the configured minimum severity.
controls.long_description: The kubelet is part of the cluster itself, so a known vulnerability in it is exposed regardless of how well the workloads are configured. Kubescape reads the kubelet version of each node from the Kubernetes API and matches it against the same vulnerability database used for image scanning. Kubernetes CVEs are attributed to a component only when the official Kubernetes CVE feed lists it as affected, so a vulnerability in another component, or one limited to another operating system, does not fail this control. Versions that cannot be assessed are reported as coverage gaps rather than as passed.
controls.remediation: Upgrade the node's kubelet to a Kubernetes patch release that fixes the listed vulnerabilities, for example by upgrading the node pool.
controls.test: Checks the vulnerabilities found for the kubelet version of each node, filtered by the configured minimum severity, fix availability and vendor build settings.

rules.name: component-vulnerabilities-kubelet

controlConfigInputs.name: Minimum severity
controlConfigInputs.description: The lowest vulnerability severity that fails the control: Negligible, Low, Medium, High or Critical.

controlConfigInputs.name: Only vulnerabilities with a fix
controlConfigInputs.description: When true, only vulnerabilities with a fixed version available fail the control.

controlConfigInputs.name: Count vendor builds
controlConfigInputs.description: When true, vulnerabilities in vendor builds (for example EKS, GKE or AKS versions) fail the control. Vendors may backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so these findings are not counted by default.

rules.description: Fails for each node whose kubelet version has known vulnerabilities at or above the configured minimum severity.
rules.remediation: Upgrade the node's kubelet to a Kubernetes patch release that fixes the listed vulnerabilities, for example by upgrading the node pool.
